newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN PRESSURED, MKT LOOKS TO CBANK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN PRESSURED, MKT LOOKS TO CBANK.

text.p: The Czech crown was under pressure in early trading on Thursday, pushing minus four percent against the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket, with some dealers suggesting the central bank may raise short term interest rates to calm sentiment.
At 0650 GMT, the crown was trading at 30.934 to the dollar and 18.229 to the mark implying a deviation from the basket mid-point of -3.91 compared with Wednesday.s fixing of -3.58 percent.
"The market feels the central bank will probably take some action...to raise the short term rates, the repo rate," said Petr Kukla of Girocredit Bank.
"I would recommend that they should do it today...market sentiment is really bad," he added.
The Czech National Bank indicated last week that it would raise interest rates to defend the crown if the need arose.
The repo rate is currently 12.4 percent while the discount rate is 10.5 percent and the last resort Lombard rate is 14 percent.
